about.intro: Calliste Travel was created for people who do not simply want to visit a place. They want to feel it.
about.storyTitle: We do not believe travel should be a checklist.
storyParagraphs: There are places you visit, photograph and forget. And then there are places that stay in your mind long after you leave.
Calliste was created around the second kind. Around small bays, quiet streets, local stories and those moments that cannot be planned down to the last minute.
That is why we carefully choose the places we share. We are not simply looking for beautiful photographs. We are looking for character.
about.ideaQuote: "The best place is not always the one everyone is already talking about."
about.ideaDescription: Travel is personal. That is why the places we look for should be special enough for everyone to create their own story.

farerski-ostrovi.title: Faroe Islands
farerski-ostrovi.excerpt: Steep cliffs, green valleys and small villages between the northern sea and the sky.
farerski-ostrovi.description: An archipelago where the weather changes within minutes and roads lead to places that feel like the end of the world. The Faroe Islands are for those who seek silence, raw nature and a feeling of true discovery.

azori.title: Azores
azori.excerpt: Volcanic islands, green craters and an ocean that seems endless.
azori.description: Far out in the Atlantic lies an archipelago where volcanic landscapes meet lush vegetation and small coastal settlements. The Azores are a place for slow exploration, long walks and days without a strict plan.

svaneti.title: Svaneti
svaneti.excerpt: Stone towers, high mountains and villages where old stories still live.
svaneti.description: In the high mountains of northern Georgia, Svaneti has preserved its medieval towers, traditions and way of life. Here, travel is not only about seeing landscapes, but about getting to know a place with its own rhythm and identity.

flores.title: Flores
flores.excerpt: Volcanic lakes, quiet coastlines and island roads that lead into the unknown.
flores.description: Flores is an island for travelers who like to move slowly and stop wherever the road looks most interesting. From the mountain landscapes to the small coastal villages, every part of the island has a different character.

raja-ampat.title: Raja Ampat
raja-ampat.excerpt: Rocky islets, turquoise water and one of the planet's most vivid marine worlds.
raja-ampat.description: Raja Ampat is an archipelago made up of hundreds of islands and small limestone formations. Instead of large tourist centers, the sea, local communities and the feeling of arriving somewhere not yet fully discovered take center stage.
highlights: Coral reefs and rich marine life

jakushima.title: Yakushima
jakushima.excerpt: Ancient forests, moss and mountain trails beneath rain that never seems to hurry.
jakushima.description: Yakushima is an island known for its ancient cedar forests and unusual, almost mystical landscape. The humid air, dense vegetation and old trees create the feeling that you have stepped into another world.

sao-tome.title: São Tomé
sao-tome.excerpt: Tropical forests, old plantations and island life far from the usual tourist routes.
sao-tome.description: The small island of São Tomé blends Portuguese heritage, African culture and tropical nature. Old plantations, green mountains and peaceful coastal settlements create a place best discovered without rushing.

karaburun.title: Karaburun
karaburun.excerpt: A wild peninsula where the mountains descend directly into the Ionian Sea.
karaburun.description: The Karaburun Peninsula is one of those parts of the Albanian coast where nature still has the final word. Rocky bays, clear water and trails above the sea make it ideal for travelers who want to explore the coast beyond the main resorts.
highlights: Hiking trails above the Ionian Sea

madeira.title: Madeira
madeira.excerpt: Green mountains, clouds beneath your feet and trails that disappear into the Atlantic.
madeira.description: Madeira is an island for those who want to spend the day outdoors and finish the evening beside the ocean. Steep mountains, levadas and old paths create endless opportunities for exploration.

utro-so-ribarite.title: Morning with the fishermen in the south
utro-so-ribarite.excerpt: Before sunrise we set out in a small wooden boat, with no plan, just a compass and curiosity.
content: Before sunrise, while the shore was still in darkness, we set out in a small wooden boat. We had no exact route and no plan for the day. Just a compass, a few coffees and curiosity.

The fishermen we went with knew the sea without looking at a map. They knew where the water changed, where the morning was calmest and where it was worth stopping even if there was nothing special to photograph.
The most interesting part of the morning was not the place we reached. It was the feeling that for a few hours we stopped checking the time and simply began following the rhythm of the sea.

seloto-bez-ime.title: The village with no name on the map
seloto-bez-ime.excerpt: Three days without internet, yet we felt more connected than we expected.
content: There was nothing special on the map. Just a small path that ended between the hills. Following it, we reached a few houses, an old stone fountain and a square small enough for all the residents to know one another.
The first thing we noticed was that the phone had no signal. The second was that nobody seemed to miss it.

We spent three days without internet. Instead of notifications, we had conversations with the villagers, homemade food and long evenings beneath the open sky. Sometimes the place that is least visible on the map is exactly the one you will remember most.

kako-da-patuvate-bavno.title: How to travel slowly instead of quickly
kako-da-patuvate-bavno.excerpt: Five lessons learned from local people about what it really means to experience a place.
content: Slow travel does not mean doing less. It means leaving enough space for something unplanned to happen.
The first lesson is not to fill every hour. Leave a morning without a plan. Walk without a specific destination. Sit in a local café and watch the day begin.
The second is to talk to local people. They often know about places, trails and stories you will never find in a tourist guide.
The third is to stay longer in one place. Instead of three cities in three days, try one city for three days.
And perhaps the most important lesson: do not try to see everything. Good travel is not a list of places you visited, but the feeling you return home with.
